p: wind: The Medes and Persians who will destroy them as the wind does the chaff.
forsaken: Though they were forsaken for a time, yet they were not utterly cast off as though their husbands were dead.
Flee from the midst of Babylon: He shows that there remains nothing for them that abide in Babylon but destruction, Jer 17:6,48:6.
LORD'S hand: By whom the Lord poured out the drink of his vengeance, to whom it pleased him.
mad: For the great afflictions that they have felt by the Babylonians.
us go every one into his: Thus the people of God exhort one another to go to Zion and praise God.
righteousness: In approving our cause and punishing our enemies.
vengeance of his temple: For the wrong done to his people and to his temple, Jer 50:28.
waters: For the land of Chaldea was full of rivers which ran into the Euphrates.
knowledge: Jer 10:14.
judgment they shall perish: When God will execute his vengeance.
portion of Jacob is not like: That is, the true God of Israel is not like these idols: for he can help when all things are desperate.
battle axe and weapons of war: He means the Medes and Persians, as before he called the Babylonians his hammer, Jer 50:23.
mountain: Not that Babylon stood on a mountain but because it was strong and seemed invincible.
rocks: From your strongholds and fortresses.
Ararat: By these three nations he means Armenia the higher, Armenia the lower and Scythia; for Cyrus had gathered an army of various nations.
one end: By turning the course of the river one side was made open and the reeds that grew in the water were destroyed which Cyrus did by the counsel of Gobria and Gabatha Belshazzar's captains.
shall come: When she will be cut up and threshed.
devoured me: This is spoken in the person of the Jews bewailing their state and the cruelty of the Babylonians.
cause: Thus the Lord esteemed the injury done to his Church as done to himself because their cause is his.
heat I will make their feasts: When they are inflamed with surfeiting and drinking, I will feast with them, alluding to Belshazzar's banquet, Da 5:2.
Sheshach taken: Meaning Babel as in Jer 25:26.
sea is come up upon Babylon: The great army of the Medes and Persians.
he hath swallowed: That is, his gifts and presents which he had received as part of the spoil of other nations, and which the idolaters brought to him from all countries.

year: Meaning that Babylon would not be destroyed all at once but little by little would be brought to nothing for the first year came the tidings, the next year the siege and in the third year it was taken: yet this is not that horrible destruction which the prophets threatened in many places: for that was after this when they rebelled and Darius over came them by the policy of Zopyrus, and hanged three thousand gentlemen beside the common people.
the earth: All creatures in heaven and earth will rejoice and praise God for the destruction of Babylon the great enemy of his Church.
slain of Israel to fall: Babylon not only destroyed Israel, but many other nations.
have escaped the sword: Yet that are now captives in Babylon.
confounded: He shows how they would remember Jerusalem by lamenting the miserable affliction of it.
heaven: For the walls were two hundred feet high.
make drunk her princes: I will so astonish them by affliction that they will not know which way to turn themselves.
broad walls of Babylon shall be: The thickness of the wall was fifty feet.
fourth year of his reign: This was not in the time of his captivity but seven years before, when he went either to congratulate Nebuchadnezzar or to intreat of some matters.
stone to it: John in his Revelation alludes to this place when he says that the angel took a millstone and cast it into the sea: signifying by it the destruction of Babylon, Re 18:21.
be weary: They will not be able to resist but will labour in vain.
